item.title: Readings
item.description:
Some of the Course Note files contain figures with associated animations or interactive simulations that can be found on the page. A table correlating the figures to the animations can be found here (PDF).

WEEK # SES # TOPICS SUMMARIES COURSE NOTES
1 1 Introduction to TEAL; Fields; Review of gravity; Electric field (PDF)

Chapter 1: Sections 1.1-1.6; 1.8 (PDF)

Chapter 2 (PDF)
2 Electric charge; Electric fields; Dipoles; Continuous charge distributions (PDF)

item.title: summary_w01d2.pdf
item.description: This file talks about concept of electric charge, and describe both how charges create electric fields and how those electric fields can in turn exert forces on other charges.

item.title: summary_w01d3.pdf
item.description: This file talks about some of the mathematical concepts and Maxwell?s equations.

item.title: summary_w02d1.pdf
item.description: This file talks about the TEAL visualizations and how to use them (with an experiment), and also talks about electric potential.

item.title: summary_w02d2.pdf
item.description: This file talks about a new way of calculating electric fields i.e. Gauss’s law.

item.title: summary_w02d3.pdf
item.description: This file talks about understanding and calculating the electric field generated by a continuous distribution of charge.

item.title: summary_w03d1.pdf
item.description: This file talks about conductors and capacitors.

item.title: summary_w03d2.pdf
item.description: This file talks about conductors & capacitors and introduces dielectrics, which are materials which when put into a capacitor decrease the electric field and hence increase the capacitance of the capacitor.

item.title: summary_w03d3.pdf
item.description: This file talks about Gauss?s Law to calculate the electric field from highly symmetric charge distributions.

item.title: summary_w04d2.pdf
item.description: This file defines current, current density, and resistance and discuss how to analyze simple DC (constant current) circuits using Kirchhoff?s Circuit Rules.

item.title: summary_w04d3.pdf
item.description: This file talks about calculating capacitance and energy storage by solving a problem and also includes a quick summary of capacitance and some notes on calculating it.

item.title: summary_w05d1.pdf
item.description: This file discusses circuits, and experiment to see what happens when capacitors are included.

item.title: summary_w05d2.pdf
item.description: This file gives a list of the expectations from the students in the examination.

item.title: summary_w06d1.pdf
item.description: This file talks about magnetism and also includes an experiment of magnetic fields of a Bar magnet and of the earth.

item.title: summary_w06d2.pdf
item.description: This resource deals with topic introduction including lorenz force on currents, field from a single moving charge, field from a current: biot-savart law, right hand rules, important equations and experiment for magnetic force on current-carrying wires.

item.title: summary_w06d3.pdf
item.description: This file talks about how to calculate the force and torque on a rectangular loop of wire and definition of the magnetic dipole moment ? and then do a calculation using that moment.

item.title: summary_w07d1.pdf
item.description: This talks about magnetic dipole moment, right hand rule for direction of dipole moment, and forces on magnetic dipole moments.

item.title: summary_w07d2.pdf
item.description: This file talks about forces on dipoles in nonuniform fields, and show some examples of using this to levitate objects. It also includes a lab to measure magnetic forces and obtain a measurement of ?0 and discusses Ampere?s Law, the magnetic equivalent of Gauss?s Law.

item.title: summary_w07d3.pdf
item.description: This file talks about calculating the magnetic field generated by a cylindrical shell of current and by a slab of current using Ampere’s law.

item.title: summary_w09d1.pdf
item.description: This resource talks about Maxwell?s equation, Faraday?s law, which explains that electric fields can be generated not only by charges but also by magnetic fields that vary in time.

item.title: summary_w09d2.pdf
item.description: This resource discusses induction (Faraday?s Law), another application ? eddy current braking ? and then continuing on to define mutual inductance and transformers.

item.title: summary_w09d3.pdf
item.description: This resource talks about Faraday?s Law to calculate the current in and force on a loop falling through a magnetic field.

item.title: summary_w10d2.pdf
item.description: This resource talks about Faraday?s Law, and move from mutual inductance, in which the changing flux from one circuit induces an EMF in another, to self inductance, in which the changing flux from a circuit induces an EMF in itself.

item.title: summary_w11d1.pdf
item.description: This resource investigates a new type of circuit ? one which consists of both capacitors and inductors.

item.title: summary_w11d2.pdf
item.description: This resource is a continuation of our investigation on LRC circuits adding a new circuit element ? the AC power supply.

item.title: summary_w11d3.pdf
item.description: This file focuses on the driven RLC circuit.

item.title: summary_w12d2.pdf
item.description: This file talks about how electricity and magnetism interact with each other and also considers finalizing Maxwell?s Equations, their result ? electromagnetic (EM) radiation and how energy flows in electric and magnetic fields.

item.title: summary_w12d3.pdf
item.description: This file deals with practicing the ideas of displacement current and the Poynting vector.

item.title: summary_w13d1.pdf
item.description: This file talks about deriving the facts about EM waves and the wave equation from the full set of Maxwell?s Equations.

item.title: summary_w14d1.pdf
item.description: This resource talks about one of the most common types of antennae, the quarter-wavelength antenna, and a lab using a type of this antenna, called the spark-gap transmitter.

item.title: summary_w14d2.pdf
item.description: Investigation on the subject of interference, both theoretically and experimentally.

item.title: visualizn_links.pdf
item.description: This resource contain the links of this course.
